data.body:
## RCA COMPLETE — confirmed root cause, and THE OUTAGE IS STILL ACTIVE

First correction to the ticket: it says 'more than 20 minutes'. I verified live just now — `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` returns **502 right now, ~4 hours in, with no self-recovery**. Discriminating probe: `/mcp` = 502 while `/review/health` = 200 and `/` = 200, so nginx, Gerrit and the review-bot are all healthy and only the rebar_mcp upstream is dead.

## Confirmed mechanism (on-box, read-only SSM)

1. **The MCP container was OOM-KILLED.** `docker inspect` on `rebar-mcp-8db373933654-8093`: `OOMKilled=true Exit=137 RestartCount=1 Status=exited`, Finished `2026-09-03T01:36:51Z` = **18:36:51 PDT**. The plan-review job started 18:31:33 PDT. **The container died ~3 minutes into the gate run.** Host is a t4g.large, 8 GiB.
2. **nginx still points at the dead port.** `/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` contains exactly `server 127.0.0.1:8093;` — the port of that exited container. A single backend, no `max_fails`/`fail_timeout`/`backup`/`proxy_next_upstream`, so one dead port is a total outage. Hence 502 rather than a connection refusal.
3. **`restart: always` did not save it** — RestartCount=1 and the container is still `exited`.

## Why it persists — recovery is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE right now

Redeploy is the only recovery path, and every attempt fails at build:

    error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`

pyproject.toml:346 pins `required-version = "==0.12.7"` while the Dockerfiles `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest`, which has moved to 0.12.9. Autodeploy is looping on this — fail#3 backoff 240s, fail#4 backoff 480s — so MCP can never rebuild. Filed separately as `febd-6b13-1976-43be` (curbable-regardable-lemming), linked, claimed, and being fixed FIRST since it is the prerequisite.

## A hypothesis I had, correctly REFUTED

I suspected `mcp_mem_abort`/`mcp_retire_cap` — the alarms I had just fixed in bff5. Both are **0.0 in every 900s bucket 15:00-21:45 PDT**, and neither has fired since 2026-08-30. They are DEPLOY-PATH markers, not observers of the serving process, so a KERNEL OOM-kill is invisible to them. Recording this because it is the interesting part: the instrumentation that exists for 'MCP ran out of memory' does not observe the case that actually happened.

## The detection gap (AC(b)) is total

`observability.sh:46-58` probes exactly two endpoints and publishes `gerrit_healthy` and `reviewbot_healthy`. There is **no `mcp_healthy` metric** — confirmed by `list-metrics` on namespace rebar/host. The container's own `/health` is not routed by any nginx location, so it is unreachable from outside the box. The deploy declares success at the flip and never re-validates. So nothing in the system can observe that /mcp is 502.

## Latent defect worth its own attention

In `autodeploy.sh`, `mcp_retire_sweep`'s live-backend guard `[ "$p" = "$live" ] && continue` sits only inside the `Running=true` branch (~line 714). An exited-but-live container falls through to the else branch and is `docker rm`'d while the nginx include still names its port — which is exactly the state observed here. That converts a transient crash into a permanent 502.

## Also noted

Root disk is back to **76% (46G/60G)** and climbing — relevant to `3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd` and epic `6202`, since the 60 GiB grow was explicitly an unwedge, not a fix.

Prior art from the search: `d240-824a-dd04-4cdb` (event-loop block, same nginx-alive/upstream-dead signature), `9d40-1db8-1bcc-4f91` (22min of 502 on the sibling /review service; its fix added a per-container healthcheck), `d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231` (added the very `review_plan_start`/`gate_status` surface in use when this broke).
